messages.subject: masked object
parts:
Getting the following message when I load ggplot2 :

library(ggplot2)
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr

Attaching package: 'reshape'

The following object(s) are masked from 'package:plyr':

round_any

Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: proto

What causes the object to be masked and is this a problem? Note that
loaded ggplot as soon as I opened my R session.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: masked object
parts:
On Sat, Feb 5, 2011 at 9:28 PM, ericstrom <eric.th...@gmail.com> wrote:
Getting the following message when I load ggplot2 :

library(ggplot2)
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr

Attaching package: 'reshape'

The following object(s) are masked from 'package:plyr':

   round_any

Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: proto

What causes the object to be masked and is this a problem? Note that
loaded ggplot as soon as I opened my R session.

What causes the masking is two or more loaded packages with the same function name. The convention in R is that the version from the most recently loaded package will be used by default. It's generally not a problem unless the function you *really* want is the one that is masked. This is not a major problem, however, because one can specify a package-function combination with a double colon in between. Here's a small example:

> x <- rnorm(5)
> plyr::round_any(x, 2)
[1]  0  0 -2  0  2
> reshape::round_any(x, 2)
[1]  0  0 -2  0  2

Preceding a function name by its package with a :: separator selects the version of the function in question in the package specified. In this case, the function round_any() is the same in both packages, as verified by checking the code in each version - the only difference between them is their namespace.

HTH,
Dennis
